props.gloss_en: on Pesach they read the portion of the festivals
and the haftara is the Pesach of Gilgal
the stam: nowadays, when there are two days, on the first day [the haftara is] the Pesach of Gilgal and on the next day the Pesach of Yoshiyahu
and on the other days of Pesach one gathers and reads from the subject of Pesach
what is it [that is read]? Rav Pappa: the mnemonic is M-A-P-V
on the last festival day of Pesach they read 'and it came to pass when [Pharaoh] sent'
and the haftara is 'and David spoke'
and on the next day, 'all the firstborn'
and the haftara is 'this very day'
Abaye: nowadays the world's practice is to read: draw-the-bull, sanctify-with-money, hew-in-the-wilderness, send-the-firstborn
on Atzeret, 'seven weeks'
and the haftara is from Chavakuk
others say: 'in the third month'
and the haftara is the Merkava
the stam: nowadays, when there are two days, we do as both, and in reverse
on Rosh HaShana, 'in the seventh month'
and the haftara is 'is Ephraim My dear son'
and some say: 'and the Lord remembered Sarah'
and the haftara is [the account of] Chana
the stam: nowadays, when there are two days -- the first day as the 'some say'; the next day, 'and God tested Abraham'
and the haftara is 'is [Ephraim] My dear son'
on Yom Kippur they read 'after the death'
and the haftara is 'for thus says the High and Lofty One'
and at mincha they read the [portion of] forbidden relations
and the haftara is Yona
R' Yochanan: wherever you find the might of the Holy One, blessed be He, you find His humility; this is written in the Torah, repeated in the Prophets and tripled in the Writings
written in the Torah: 'for the Lord your God is God of gods and Lord of lords', and after it: 'He executes justice for the orphan and the widow'
repeated in the Prophets: 'thus says the High and Lofty One who inhabits eternity, whose name is holy', and after it: 'and with the contrite and lowly of spirit'
tripled in the Writings: 'extol Him who rides upon the heavens, whose name is Yah', and after it: 'father of orphans and judge of widows'
on the first festival day of the Chag they read the portion of the festivals in Torat Kohanim
and the haftara is 'behold, a day of the Lord comes'
the stam: nowadays, when there are two days, on the next day we read the same Torah portion
the stam: what is the haftara? -- 'and they assembled to King Shlomo'
and on all the other days of the Chag they read the offerings of the Chag
on the last festival day they read 'all the firstborn' -- mitzvot and statutes and firstborn
and the haftara is 'and it was when Shlomo finished'
the next day they read 'and this is the blessing'
and the haftara is 'and Shlomo stood'
Shabbat that falls in the intermediate days, whether of Pesach or of Sukkot -- the Torah reading is 'see, You [say to me]'
the haftara, on Pesach -- the dry bones
and on Sukkot -- 'on the day Gog comes'
on Chanukah -- the Nesi'im
and the haftara is the lamps of Zecharya
the stam: and if two Shabbatot occur -- the first, the lamps of Zecharya
the stam: the latter, the lamps of Shlomo
on Purim -- 'and Amalek came'
on Rashei Chodashim -- 'and on your new moons'
Rosh Chodesh that falls on Shabbat: the haftara is 'and it shall be, new moon after new moon'
if it falls on the first day of the week, on the day before the haftara is 'and Yehonatan said to him: tomorrow is the new moon'
Rav Huna: Rosh Chodesh Av that falls on Shabbat -- the haftara is 'your new moons and your festivals My soul hates; they are a burden upon Me'
the stam: what is 'they are a burden upon Me'? -- the Holy One said: it is not enough for Israel that they sin before Me, but they burden Me to know which harsh decree I shall bring upon them
on the Ninth of Av itself, what is the haftara? Rav: 'how has [the faithful city] become a harlot'
what is the Torah reading? It was taught: others say, 'and if you will not listen to Me'
R' Natan bar Yosef says: 'how long will this people provoke Me'
and some say: 'how long [shall I bear] with this evil congregation'
Abaye: nowadays the world's practice is to read 'when you beget children'
and the haftara is 'I will utterly consume them'
